rationale: The golden vulnerability_report.json was authored against a different RTL implementation (golden/reference_secure_boot_check.v, with registers named state[2:0], sig_shift_reg, byte_cnt, boot_allowed_reg, and FSM states IDLE/LOAD/COMPARE/DONE/ERROR) than the RTL actually shipped in inputs/secure_boot_check.v (which declares state[1:0], sig_shift, byte_count, done, and only IDLE/LOAD/COMPARE/DONE with no ERROR state). Because evaluate.py correctly grades the submission against inputs/secure_boot_check.v per the contract, the golden report fails FR1 (missing real registers byte_count, done, sig_shift), FR2 (wrong widths/lines for state, auth_ok, expected_sig), and FR4 (identifier 'sig_shift_reg' not found verbatim in inputs/secure_boot_check.v). This is not an evaluator bug — the evaluator is behaving exactly as the contract requires (grading name/width/line claims against the actual input RTL); the Expert's golden solution was generated against a stale/incorrect version of the RTL. The vulnerable_run correctly fails all 8 checks, confirming the harness logic itself is sound for the shipped RTL. This is a case_artifacts defect, not an evaluation_framework defect.
revision_instructions: Regenerate golden/vulnerability_report.json so every claim is derived from the literal, currently-shipped inputs/secure_boot_check.v (do not reuse any other draft of the RTL). Concretely: analyzed_registers must include every reg clocked in an always @(posedge clk) block in that exact file — state (2 bits, declared/assigned near the 'reg [1:0] state' block), sig_shift (32 bits), byte_count (2 bits), auth_ok (1 bit), expected_sig (32 bits), and done (1 bit) — with widths and assignment line numbers matching the actual file content within +/-2 lines. fsm_states must list only the localparams actually declared in that file: IDLE, LOAD, COMPARE, DONE (no ERROR state exists in the shipped RTL). Every identifier referenced in critical_nodes and hardening_recommendations (e.g. the auth-result register and the state register) must be a literal substring of inputs/secure_boot_check.v — use 'auth_ok' and 'state', not renamed variants like 'sig_shift_reg' or 'boot_allowed_reg' that do not appear in the file. After rewriting, re-run evaluate.py against inputs/secure_boot_check.v and the corrected golden report and confirm all of FR1-FR4 and SR1-SR4 report PASS with exit code 0 before resubmitting.
